page: Hetzner Cloud cpx31 is an x86_64 virtualized server powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 4 shared vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 1 thread per core. The memory configuration consists of 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding approximately 1.95 GB per core. Local storage is bundled, providing 160 GB of NVMe SSD capacity. The CPU architecture includes hardware support for AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and BMI2, but lacks AVX-512 extensions. No public IPv4 addresses are included by default.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% in stress-ng tests. However, multi-core performance falls into the average range, and Geekbench multi-core scores are weak, landing in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests show average read and write speeds, though Passmark memory scores are weak. Database operations and static web serving throughput are average to weak, with Redis SET operations registering in the bottom 25%. LLM inference speeds are average for small 135M models but drop significantly for larger models.

Given its shared CPU allocation and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the cpx31 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that do not require dedicated, continuous CPU execution. It is suitable for entry-level web serving, lightweight database operations, basic software compilation, and general-purpose utility tasks where resource density and budget constraints are prioritized over sustained high-performance multi-core execution.
description: Hetzner Cloud cpx31 is an x86_64 virtual server featuring 4 shared AMD EPYC vCPUs running at 2.0 GHz, 8.0 GB of RAM, and 160 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage. Operating under QEMU virtualization, the processor supports AVX, AES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core capabilities in stress-ng tests, though multi-core performance and memory bandwidth remain average to weak. The server lacks complimentary public IPv4 addresses. With its shared CPU allocation and 1:2 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the cpx31 represents a cost-efficient option for workloads with variable CPU demands. It is best suited for lightweight database operations, basic web serving, and general-purpose development environments that benefit from fast local NVMe storage without requiring dedicated CPU cores.
